summary.intent: Run the full post-execute pipeline for GSD phase 66 (API schema cutover, IPNS publish gate, tombstone) autonomously: verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E → CodeRabbit CLI → ship PR → resolve reviews → confirm green CI.
summary.outcome: PR #584 opened and pushed to green CI across all jobs. Security fix T-66-E1 applied, 19 CodeRabbit threads + 2 greptile threads resolved, Test 15 removed from sdk-e2e and replaced with unit tests, 8 deferred todos captured. Final merge decision left to user.

repo: The CI sdk-e2e job started mock-ipns-routing with `node dist/server.js` but the package entry is `dist/index.js` — a phantom file that silently crashed behind `&` + `sleep 2` since PR #318. This was the root cause of Test 15 failing in CI; the server has never run in CI.

THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET must be set on the API process, not just the test step. In CI the API starts without it so the bypass header silently fails and per-IP throttling fires under the full E2E suite load; the correct fix is `NODE_ENV=test` early return in the guard.

Phase 66 deleted all shares specs but left their jest per-file coverage thresholds — shares controllers dropped to 0%, global branches to 74.73% (<78%), causing the CI Test job to fail with threshold violations (not test failures).
jest `coverageThreshold` path-specific entries are SUBTRACTED from the global computation, so EXIT=0 is authoritative even when the 'All files' summary row shows a number below the global gate.

The `api:generate` trailing `eslint .` step trips on pre-existing gitignored generated files (`landing/.astro/*`, `ipfs/...`) and exits 1, but the actual OpenAPI artifacts regenerate cleanly — the exit code is not a reliable signal here.
The `chore(release)` bot commit pushes to the branch after both `gh pr create` and after a passing Release Preview — must `git fetch` + rebase before every subsequent push or the push is rejected.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — all PR body updates must go via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
GSD secure-phase and validate-phase step hooks can be disabled in config; the workflow still runs the audit directly when no active hook exists (State B mode).

The `BypassableThrottlerGuard` uses a per-IP tracker by default, so in CI all localhost requests share one bucket and heavy suites exhaust per-route `@Throttle` limits (e.g. resolve = 30/min), causing 429s that the SDK surfaces as null.
The migration file (`ApiSchemaCutover.ts`) acquired prettier drift through automated commits that bypass the local hook — CI Lint catches it on the repo-wide `eslint .` run.

code.finding: T-66-E1: write grant was derived from claimer input (`dto.writeDescriptorRef`) without checking `invite.writeDescriptorRef !== null`. A read-only invite could yield a write share if the claimer supplied a writeDescriptorRef. Fixed by gating on `inviteGrantsWrite = invite.writeDescriptorRef !== null`.

SeqFloor resolve gate: when `signedRecord` is null, the resolve returns a `SeqFloor` discriminant. The gate checks `networkSeq >= floor` before serving — below-floor fails closed. This is pure comparison logic that belongs in unit tests, not a live-stack e2e that needs psql seeding.
When both the cached record and network record are null/unparseable, the function returns null (fail-closed). No ungated fallthrough.

The idempotent republish test deliberately uses a different CID at the same sequence number and asserts `latestCid` updates — this is the D-09 / Pitfall 4 TEE re-sign design. CodeRabbit's finding [5] (reject same-seq different-CID) would reverse this deliberate invariant; deferred as a separate todo.

Added `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test') { return true; }` at the top of `canActivate` to disable all rate limiting in the test environment. Staging and production still use the header+secret bypass path.
SDK E2E job started mock-ipns-routing with `node dist/server.js` (phantom file) instead of `node dist/index.js`. Fixed and added a `/health` poll so a dead server fails loudly instead of silently.
syncIpnsRecordSequence lacked `tombstonedAt: IsNull()` in its update criteria, meaning a concurrent republish during the TEE race window could bump a tombstoned row's sequence back to active.

Test 15 (TEE-05 seqFloor) reached a precondition (null `signedRecord` at a chosen floor) that is impossible to create through the publish API — it required psql to set `signed_record = NULL`. This is white-box coupling and the behaviors are already covered by unit tests; removed in favour of 3 new unit tests in ipns.service.spec.ts.

workflow: The 5-agent Workflow fan-out for parallel spec authoring (disjoint files, no write conflicts) was effective; adversarially verifying subagent results with a central jest run caught spec drift before committing.
The commit helper (1Password signing) frequently times out (exit 143) while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` and never retry blindly.
CodeRabbit re-reviews every push and raises new findings on fix commits — budget time for a second triage round after addressing the first batch.

CodeRabbit 'outside of diff range' findings appear in issue-comment bodies, not as resolvable review threads, so a `reviewThreads` GraphQL sweep misses them — requires scanning issue comments separately.
The zsh `status` variable is reserved; using it as a loop variable in a background poll caused an exit-1 that looked like a CI failure.

Direct DB seeding in e2e tests is a smell when the precondition is unreachable through the public API — it white-box-couples the test to the physical schema and introduces propagation timing dependencies. Prefer unit tests for pure logic gates.

friction: The real SDK E2E root cause (phantom `server.js` CI entry) was masked by a red herring (throttle 429s) for multiple iterations, requiring several CI cycles to isolate.
The mock-ipns-routing server silently never ran in CI since PR #318 — the `&` + `sleep 2` pattern completely suppressed the startup failure, giving no diagnostic signal.
1Password commit signing timed out (exit 143) on nearly every commit while the commit actually landed, requiring a `git log` verify step after every commit.
The greptile 'outside of diff range' finding was not surfaced by the automated thread sweep and required the user to manually point it out via a direct URL.

The `gsd-context-monitor.js` and `gsd-check-update.js` hooks used relative paths in settings.local.json — any Bash command that `cd`s into a subdir caused a `cjs/loader:1433` error on every tool call, generating constant noise.
CodeRabbit CLI first run failed with 'Active connection is not open' and had to be retried.
The `api:generate` step exits 1 due to pre-existing gitignored generated files even when the real artifacts regenerate correctly, making it unreliable as a success signal.
Phase 66's automated executor commits bypassed the pre-commit prettier hook on the migration file, causing CI Lint to fail on a commit I didn't author.
